name: java-springboot
description: Spring Boot development best practices.
Help write high-quality Spring Boot applications.

- Use Maven (`pom.xml`) or Gradle (`build.gradle`) for dependency management and Spring Boot starters (e.g., `spring-boot-starter-web`, `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa`).
- Organize code by feature/domain (e.g., `com.example.app.order`) rather than layer.
- Always use constructor-based injection for required dependencies.
- Declare dependency fields `private final`.
- Use `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, and `<REDACTED_USER>`/`<REDACTED_USER>` annotations appropriately to define beans.
- Configure with `application.yml` (or `application.properties`); use `<REDACTED_USER>` for type-safe configuration. Use Spring Profiles (`application-dev.yml`, `application-prod.yml`) for environment-specific configuration.
- Do not hardcode secrets. Use environment variables or a dedicated secret management tool like HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager.
- Design consistent RESTful endpoints. Use DTOs in the API layer. Do not expose JPA entities directly to the client. Validate DTO request payloads with Java Bean Validation (JSR 380) annotations (`<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`).
- Implement global exception handling using `<REDACTED_USER>` and `<REDACTED_USER>`.
- Encapsulate business logic in `<REDACTED_USER>` classes; services should be stateless. Use `<REDACTED_USER>` on service methods for declarative transactions, at the most granular necessary level.
- Extend `JpaRepository` or `CrudRepository` for standard Spring Data JPA operations. For complex queries, use `<REDACTED_USER>` or JPA Criteria API. Use DTO projections to fetch only necessary data.
- Use SLF4J. Logger declaration: `private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MyClass.class);` Use parameterized messages (`logger.info("Processing us
